packages.name: com.landawn.abacus.util

methods.javadoc_summary: Flattens a two-dimensional array, performs an in-place operation on the resulting one-dimensional array, and then copies the modified elements back into the original two-dimensional array.
contract: Changes made directly to `a` by the action are not rolled back if it throws.
For a nonempty outer array, the action is invoked once even when all nested arrays are null or empty.
Rows are copied back in index order; if multiple positions reference the same row, the last copy wins.
If the action replaces nested arrays through another reference to `a`, their new structure determines where the flat elements are copied.
If the updated rows need fewer elements, the unused suffix of the flat array is discarded.
⚠️ Size limit: If the logical element count exceeds `Integer.MAX_VALUE`, this method throws `ArithmeticException` before invoking the action or copying elements back.

methods.javadoc_summary: Flattens a two-dimensional array, performs an in-place operation on the resulting one-dimensional array, and then copies the modified elements back into the original two-dimensional array.
contract: Changes made directly to `a` by the action are not rolled back if it throws.
For a nonempty outer array, the action is invoked once even when all nested arrays are null or empty.
Rows are copied back in index order; if multiple positions reference the same row, the last copy wins.
If the action replaces nested arrays through another reference to `a`, their new structure determines where the flat elements are copied.
If the updated rows need fewer elements, the unused suffix of the flat array is discarded.
⚠️ Size limit: If the logical element count exceeds `Integer.MAX_VALUE`, this method throws `ArithmeticException` before invoking the action or copying elements back.

methods.javadoc_summary: Flattens a two-dimensional array, performs an in-place operation on the resulting one-dimensional array, and then copies the modified elements back into the original two-dimensional array.
contract: Changes made directly to `a` by the action are not rolled back if it throws.
For a nonempty outer array, the action is invoked once even when all nested arrays are null or empty.
Rows are copied back in index order; if multiple positions reference the same row, the last copy wins.
If the action replaces nested arrays through another reference to `a`, their new structure determines where the flat elements are copied.
If the updated rows need fewer elements, the unused suffix of the flat array is discarded.
⚠️ Size limit: If the logical element count exceeds `Integer.MAX_VALUE`, this method throws `ArithmeticException` before invoking the action or copying elements back.

methods.javadoc_summary: Flattens a two-dimensional array, performs an in-place operation on the resulting one-dimensional array, and then copies the modified elements back into the original two-dimensional array.
contract: Changes made directly to `a` by the action are not rolled back if it throws.
For a nonempty outer array, the action is invoked once even when all nested arrays are null or empty.
Rows are copied back in index order; if multiple positions reference the same row, the last copy wins.
If the action replaces nested arrays through another reference to `a`, their new structure determines where the flat elements are copied.
If the updated rows need fewer elements, the unused suffix of the flat array is discarded.
⚠️ Size limit: If the logical element count exceeds `Integer.MAX_VALUE`, this method throws `ArithmeticException` before invoking the action or copying elements back.

methods.javadoc_summary: Flattens a two-dimensional array, performs an in-place operation on the resulting one-dimensional array, and then copies the modified elements back into the original two-dimensional array.
contract: Changes made directly to `a` by the action are not rolled back if it throws.
For a nonempty outer array, the action is invoked once even when all nested arrays are null or empty.
Rows are copied back in index order; if multiple positions reference the same row, the last copy wins.
If the action replaces nested arrays through another reference to `a`, their new structure determines where the flat elements are copied.
If the updated rows need fewer elements, the unused suffix of the flat array is discarded.

methods.javadoc_summary: Flattens a two-dimensional array, performs an in-place operation on the resulting one-dimensional array, and then copies the modified elements back into the original two-dimensional array.
contract: Changes made directly to `a` by the action are not rolled back if it throws.
For a nonempty outer array, the action is invoked once even when all nested arrays are null or empty.
Rows are copied back in index order; if multiple positions reference the same row, the last copy wins.
If the action replaces nested arrays through another reference to `a`, their new structure determines where the flat elements are copied.
If the updated rows need fewer elements, the unused suffix of the flat array is discarded.

methods.signature: public static <T> T[] flatten(final T[][] a) throws IllegalArgumentException, ArithmeticException

params.name: a
params.javadoc: the two-dimensional array to flatten (must not be `null`).

throws.condition: if `a` is `null`.
if the logical element count exceeds `Integer.MAX_VALUE`.

methods.javadoc_summary: Flattens a two-dimensional array into a one-dimensional array by concatenating all sub-arrays.
methods.returns: a one-dimensional array containing all elements from the input array, newly allocated unless it is empty (an empty result may be a shared zero-length array, for example when the component type is `Object`, `String`, or a primitive wrapper). Its component type is obtained by removing two array dimensions from the runtime type of `a`; any additional dimensions belonging to `T` remain intact. This type may be narrower than `T`; storing an incompatible value in the result throws `ArrayStoreException`.
contract: ⚠️ Size limit: If the logical element count exceeds `Integer.MAX_VALUE`, this method throws `ArithmeticException` before allocating the result array.

methods.name: mutateViaFlatArray
methods.signature: public static <T, E extends Exception> void mutateViaFlatArray(final T[][] a, final Throwables.Consumer<? super T[], E> action) throws IllegalArgumentException, ArithmeticException, E, IndexOutOfBoundsException, ArrayStoreException

params.name: a
params.javadoc: the two-dimensional array to operate on (can be `null` or empty). The operation modifies this array in-place.

params.name: action
params.javadoc: the consumer that operates on the flattened array (must not be `null`).

throws.condition: if `action` is `null`.
if the logical element count exceeds `Integer.MAX_VALUE`.
if the `action` throws an exception.
if the action changes the input structure so that copying the flattened elements into its current rows requires more elements than the temporary array contains.

if the action stores an incompatible value in the temporary array, or a value cannot be stored when copied back to a destination row. The temporary array's component type is obtained by removing two dimensions from the runtime type of `a`; it may be wider than an individual row's component type. Copying back can partially modify the input: rows copied before the failure retain their new values, as does the assignable prefix of the failing row.

methods.javadoc_summary: Performs an operation on a temporary flat copy of a two-dimensional array, then copies the modified elements back to the original array structure.

methods.name: sum

methods.name: sum
methods.javadoc_summary: Returns the sum of all double values in this tuple.
methods.returns: the sum of all double values in this tuple, or `0.0` if empty
contract: If any element is not finite, the result is the IEEE-754 sum of the non-finite elements alone: `NaN` if any is `NaN` or both infinities occur, otherwise that infinity.

Finite elements never turn an infinity of a single sign into `NaN`, even when they overflow toward the opposite sign: `DoubleTuple.of(Double.MAX_VALUE, Double.MAX_VALUE, Double.NEGATIVE_INFINITY).sum()` is `-Infinity`.
This differs from `N.sum(double...)` and `DoubleStream.sum()`, which return `NaN` when such an overflow precedes the infinity.
If that compensated result is not finite although every element is finite (the compensation term itself can overflow, e.g.

for `DoubleTuple.of(-3.0E307, Double.MAX_VALUE)`), the exact total is recomputed and rounded once, so an infinity is returned only when the exact total is outside the `double` range; `DoubleStream.sum()` does not recompute and returns `-Infinity` for that example.

methods.name: average
methods.javadoc_summary: Returns the arithmetic mean of all double values in this tuple.
methods.returns: the arithmetic mean of all double values in this tuple as an `OptionalDouble`, or an empty `OptionalDouble` if this tuple is empty
contract: If any element is `NaN`, the mean is `NaN`.
This differs from `N.average(double...)` and `DoubleStream.average()`, which return `NaN` when such an overflow precedes the infinity.
If the compensated total overflows, the mean is recovered from the exact values of all elements before division and rounding.

When the computed (rounded) total is negative and the mean underflows to zero, the result is `-0.0`, as in `DoubleTuple.of(-Double.MIN_VALUE, 0.0).average().getAsDouble()`; a computed total of zero gives `+0.0`, even when compensation loses a tiny negative term, as in `DoubleTuple.of(-1.0, -Double.MIN_VALUE, 1.0)`, whose exact total is `-Double.MIN_VALUE`.

contract: Returns `true` if and only if the specified object is also an ImmutableIntArray and both arrays contain the same elements in the same order.

contract: If the true total exceeds the range of `long`, the result wraps around according to standard two's-complement long arithmetic rather than throwing an exception.

contract: When no prefix overflows, the exact total is narrowed to `double` and then divided.
When a prefix does overflow, a quotient/remainder decomposition is used instead.

This path can round twice even when the arity is a power of two: `LongTuple.of(Long.MAX_VALUE, 1026L).average().getAsDouble()` returns `4.611686018427388E18`, while the nearest `double` is `4.611686018427389E18`.
Adding a rounded fraction to a quotient can also leave the result tens of ulps off when large elements very nearly cancel.
